plan: This is a single-round auction, so long-term profit maximization simplifies to maximizing profit in this round. In a second-price auction with rational bidders, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy. This is because bidding below your value risks losing a profitable auction, and bidding above your value risks winning an auction at a loss. Since my value is $39, I will bid $39.

I need to maximize my profit. Since I pay the second-highest bid, I want to bid as high as possible to win, but not so high that my profit is negative. My value is $34. I will bid slightly above what I anticipate the other bidders might bid, while ensuring I still make a profit. Given the value range of $0-$49, and that other bidders are rational, they will likely bid below their value. I will bid slightly below my value to ensure a positive profit if I win, but high enough to be competitive.

This is a first-price sealed-bid auction with a second-price payment rule (Vickrey auction). In such auctions, the dominant strategy is to bid your true value. Bidding less risks losing to a lower bid, and bidding more risks overpaying if you win. Since my value is $45, I will bid $45.
